[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] Digital Realty is a publicly traded data center real estate investment trust. This session sourced two acquisitions that explain building names appearing across this operators rows in this registry. Per Data Center Dynamics trade press, Digital Realty completed a 7.8 billion dollar all-stock merger with DuPont Fabros Technology on September 15, 2017, adding 12 facilities concentrated in Ashburn, Virginia, which is why several Ashburn buildings in this registry still carry DuPont Fabros own ACC, meaning Ashburn Corporate Campus, naming convention. Separately, per Data Center Knowledge trade press, Digital Realty acquired the East Coast data center operations of AboveNet Inc. on October 2, 2006, for 40 million dollars, including a leased facility at 8100 Boone Boulevard, Vienna, Virginia, which is this registrys 8100 Boone Boulevard row. This specific row, 8100 Boone Boulevard, traces directly to the October 2, 2006 AboveNet acquisition sourced above: per Data Center Knowledge trade press, this leased facility at 8100 Boone Boulevard, Vienna, VA came to Digital Realty as one of three East Coast AboveNet data centers acquired that day for 40 million dollars, alongside a New York City carrier hotel and a separate Reston, VA property not tracked as a row in this registry. A DataCenterMap listing corroborates the facility remains active at this address today, labeled Vienna, VA.

reading.body:
This facility at 8100 Boone Boulevard in Vienna is part of Digital Realty's Northern Virginia campus, one of the largest concentrations of colocation buildings in Data Center Alley. The campus spans multiple municipalities and includes at least six named buildings with confirmed street addresses. The individual critical IT megawatt capacity of this specific building is not published.

Virginia has 326 mapped data center facilities, of which 23 publish power capacity figures totaling 1,375 megawatts. This campus does not appear among the top 23 published capacity rankings in the state by announced megawatts, placing it outside the tier of facilities with disclosed power specifications.

The building traces to Digital Realty's October 2006 acquisition of AboveNet Inc. and has remained in operation at this leased address for nearly two decades. Without published specifications for this building, its relevance to AI scaling depends on whether Digital Realty has upgraded its infrastructure since acquisition or disclosed capacity figures through channels this site has not yet indexed.
